Question: Which isotopic pair is most likely to exhibit the largest isotope effect?

Options:
A. Carbon-12 and carbon-13
B. Carbon-12 and carbon-14
C. Hydrogen and deuterium
D. Nitrogen-14 and nitrogen-15

Thought: The isotope effect refers to the change in the behavior of a molecule when one of its atoms is replaced by one of its isotopes. This effect is most pronounced when there is a significant difference in the mass of the isotopes. Hydrogen and deuterium have the largest relative difference in mass compared to the other options, as hydrogen (protium) has a mass of 1, while deuterium has a mass of 2. The other isotope pairs have much smaller relative mass differences. Therefore, the isotopic pair of hydrogen and deuterium is most likely to exhibit the largest isotope effect.
